title: Choose starting-state and prove reset deliberately
when: Before scheduling QA that resets a host
need: A dedicated baseline needs golden capture plus restore proof, not just SSH or a saved archive. Verify/reset are destructive provisioning operations. No baseline is also a supported no-reset posture; an as_is case needs a reason. Capacity-machine registration is separate from test-machine registration. A nonzero native baseline probe retains its diagnosed quota, authentication, model or transport cause. Quota and unknown failures preserve the golden and do not justify sign-in or credential resets; authentication recovery needs actual native evidence. Linux reset must keep desktop Chromium sign-ins live outside goldens, preserve ~/snap/chromium/common/chromium only when present, never restore stale sign-in state from an older golden, and stop Chromium before preservation to flush its state. Require separate real reset and browser sign-in proof against the selected release. On Ubuntu24.04, Codex sandbox recovery audits the actual denied executable, grants userns only to that exact helper while retaining the global restriction at1, and requires ordinary sandbox command exit0/output in the same human-opened session plus fresh audit inspection. Re-audit after helper updates; renewed denial or missing helper blocks provisioning.
surface: Per-OS capture/verify/reset; machine setting optional baseline; Pack starting-state contract. Current Linux golden-home reference and Machine QA Linux baseline capture/recovery procedure.
gap: The entry guide must explain when a resettable rig is necessary. Do not make every browser user build a clean-install lab or mistake capacity registration for QA readiness.
review: Pending exact live recipe proof. Earlier producer evidence was 29 targeted PASS, CI run 39040788218 PASS and QA requirement 50631 artifact 36759. Real reset/sign-in and released proof remain pending. Superseded opt-in source e2dc611a21d52f4e192d7e18eb3804d8dd45c5d3 passed full CI run 39044050221; that passing opt-in contract is not the final landed default-inclusion behavior. Final source landed at merge 9768e3e8e225ed4120d2251eac4587ea6aa4ddd0, whose source parent is 6fd8127f13e7e3fa3779d9d3ca7647881dac46d7. Its verified browser_authorize_help.py and routing include selected automation plus native Linux snap Chromium/macOS Safari by default with --machine, using declared sites/accounts, headless native cookies, expired-only tabs and named accounts; unreadable cookies/unreachable probes refuse before tabs. No remote desktop opt-out exists. Without --machine local automation stays unchanged; standalone --desktop-browser checks native local only. Desktop reset refuses and remote --reset affects only automation. Producer full CI run 39045367272 PASS on exact source 6fd8127f13e7e3fa3779d9d3ca7647881dac46d7, QA requirement 50674 artifact 36808, followed one steering-authorized unchanged-index-flake rerun with the original failure retained. This is merged source/full-gate evidence, not released delivery or actual authorize/reset/live proof; those remain pending. Scoped sandbox recovery has producer-reported actual proof on requirement 49008, QA run 50474, artifacts 36760 and 36761: same-session ordinary sandbox command exit0/output, scoped profile and global sysctl1. This proves that recovery only; overall installer and released recipe proof remain pending. A later api.upyoke.com DNS restriction is a separate blocker, not an AppArmor failure.
